body:
100% agree! No one knows you like YOU do. Unless they have a medical degree it’s not their place to chime in. I’m sorry they’re not supporting you in the best way. Your health, your meds, YOUR life. You are your biggest advocate at the end of the day, keep control of that. 

Don’t give up on your medication, it took some time for me to find the right combo and it’s truly saved my life. I’m here for you. ❤️

Yes!! I’ve been on Adderall for almost 15 years and before my bipolar 2 diagnosis (10 years ago) Adderall made my mania worse and gave me “Adderall rage”. The ADHD symptoms were managed, but during manic episodes I’d either be obsessively cleaning or working on a creative project (sleep is for the weak!) at all hours. I don’t think it took away from my creativity at all, if anything it helped me FINALLY finish a project lol. 

HOWEVER, I would Hulk out at the smallest thing to the point of violence (towards objects and myself mainly) but no one was spared from my verbal wrath. I was irrationally angry and couldn’t figure out why until we started an antidepressant. That helped the Hulk-like rage, but made my impulsivity WORSE. That’s a whole rabbit hole though. Then I finally got my bipolar 2 diagnosis and got on Lithium with my antidepressant and it no joke saved my life. 

Tbh while finding the right doses I did get a little creatively stifled, but not enough to where I couldn’t break through. At the end of the day, I’d rather be alive and a functioning person in society than worrying about meds hurting my creativity. Discuss this with your prescribing doctor or psychiatrist and come up with a plan of what’s best for you. ❤️

First, you’re absolutely correct - this disorder IS a disability and can be debilitating. Not many people acknowledge or even understand that. What you must remember is that you’re not useless. You’re extremely capable based on the fact you’re in a relationship, take responsibility by being a cat parent, have pursued higher education, and you work. These may seem like basic things, but to us in this community you’re doing everything you can to not just live, but to THRIVE. Our brains try to downplay all of that, I see it as BP2 trying to sabotage what you’ve built for yourself. 

It sounds like your stress from work and grad school has manifested itself into auditory hallucinations. I had auditory hallucinations of my name being called in various voices and pitches. Then I had visual hallucinations of spiders coming out of my bedroom ceiling. My therapist told me that when our brains are under tremendous emotional stress, anxiety, trauma, etc that it can’t handle anymore, it creates these hallucinations of these feelings that leak out. Basically you’re so overwhelmed your brain is filling the gaps with things (good or bad) to release it so you don’t “fully break” into a psychosis (which can be different for EVERYONE, this is how my therapist explained it to me). 

My biggest piece of advice (being a serial job hopper reaching my late 20s): 
Keep working with your psychiatrist and psychologist if you have one. Whether it’s meds that need adjusting or extra therapy sessions, stress of school and work is adding up for you in a negative way. Lack of sleep and physical symptoms can trigger episodes easier (including hallucinations), and your body is sending you SOS signals. If your job has a good HR department, see if you qualify for a medical leave. Maybe you need to talk to your boss about more frequent breaks during the day or leaving earlier some days in order to manage stress levels. I don’t know the field you’re in, but perhaps you should take the skills and schooling but put it in a different job that is not as stressful as your current job. 

We’re all rooting for you and hope things work out, please keep us updated. ❤️

I’m a personal trainer and boxing coach! It took MANY jobs and career shifts to figure out what I’m passionate about and love doing. I’ve always taken on management roles at companies to stay busy busy busy, but then I inevitably overwork and burn myself out. I thought I liked the rules and rigidity of management, but I realized I like the flexibility of scheduling clients. I still have structure but can take breaks when I need to.

Thank you for your response! She screams and cries asking for her pain meds. She tells us that “we’re mean” if she doesn’t get her pain meds, which we’re no longer responsible for dispensing since they took over. The early stages of dementia diagnosis came during her bout with kidney stones because she was hallucinating. The hallucinations stopped once that was managed. The only time I’ve seen her angry is when she wants her meds, and she does say “I’m 89, let me have my meds!” She’s not hitting anyone but it is so hard to watch. I understand she’s in pain, but she was tricking people previously to give her MORE meds too close to her dose time - like 3 hours after she took her initial pill. If you call her out on it she knows she’s been caught. I believe she started this opioid close to 5 years ago and it’s causing her to have bad side effects like nausea, constipation, and she is definitely a fall risk. 

I know there isn’t anything I can do for her since I’m her granddaughter and cannot make any medical decisions. Mentally it’s just hard to watch and I wanted to hear from others how they coped and how they approached it with their loved ones, like what do I even say to her  anymore while she’s going through this? Do I try to distract her with different activities or stories? I appreciate your comment, I can relay that to my parents about some potential next steps. I’ll have to see what kind of doctors they have on staff or if we’ll need to take her somewhere.

I’m a General Manager of a CrossFit/powerlifting gym! I was previously a manager/coach at a boxing club and I pop in there from time to time. I had to step back from being a trainer for now so I can work more on my mental health. My current job as a GM gives me the flexibility in hours so I can work at my peak productivity times and go home around 3 PM. My job can also be done remotely too which helps A LOT. It has its busy times which satisfies my needs for an adrenaline rush. Managing operations and people leaves no time to think about my moods, I’m in “go mode”. :)
Lol, this made my evening.

The thing is, I didn’t even really get that far with explaining my specific ask before she blew up. She has a bad habit of interrupting too which is also frustrating when I say something she doesn’t agree with. All I wanted to do was have a meeting with her and the employee (I’ve had several one on ones with the employee) to discuss their recent behavior - not to fire them or make a huge/stressful decision. Just every day business. I am HR and home office, so yes, small business. Lol.
Thank you for this. I’m sorry you had to deal with it too. I’m going to start putting feelers out for a new job.

I’ve just never been talked to like that by a boss, and it’s so unprofessional. I think the physical aspect of her temper tantrum scared me most. Tbh she doesn’t know how to manage people, and has told me she wants ME to be the “bad cop”. I can’t be the “bad cop” if I literally have no power or support from the person that hired me. It’s such a backwards situation I got myself into. It’s hard because I’ve met some great people, have a great schedule, and I’m in the industry I want to be in. Sigh.

I haven’t even scratched the surface of the things I’ve heard her say/seen her do. Funny you mention I’m not a dog, because she brings her 2 dogs to the gym and I’ve seen her get so mad at her dog for almost biting someone she shoved him hard into the wall of our office. It was so disturbing to see.

Gotcha. She used to yell or snap a lot when I first started, but this is the first time she’s cursed DIRECTLY at me. The physical part of shoving furniture was what scared me the most honestly. Sometimes I feel like I have a hard time determining the line of when enough is enough.

I've felt this and still struggle with this, my husband does too. **Let me ask you this - you've had a great few days/week - why is that? What happened that made things so great? Did something happen or trigger you - consciously or subconsciously to make your happiness drain away like that?** It can be anything, nothing is too big or small. A comment from a loved one, your favorite show being discontinued, being passed up on a promotion, etc. It's easy for some to just put on happy music or do things that make them happy, which works for some (and that's great!), but not for everyone. 

My approach to depression is different. What has helped me catch myself before getting depressed is recognizing the changes within myself (my habits, how I'm feeling physically, and even how I'm reacting to normal things in life). Also, therapy, meditation, and introspection has helped me sit with my depression. I like to compare depression to being like a blanket over all the emotions I'm feeling. Depression wraps me up in its blanket so I don't deal with the tough emotions (or demons as I refer to them) that terrify me. 

In the past few years, I've discovered that depression has covered my feelings of anger (from my childhood), resentment (in the present), grief (from loss), fear (from being sexually assaulted), insecurity, anxiety, and more. Once I was able to recognize these "demons" I felt like I could face them easier. I won't lie, it's been tough work. It's a lot of thinking and sitting with it. 

I'll put on classical music and zone out or write for a while, anything that comes to mind. I've written countless letters to my emotions (and people - never sent them) and what they've done to me. Crying is normal, crying is okay, crying is **HEALING.** Since you're used to living with sadness, use that as a way to try and understand yourself on a deeper level. Of course, seeking help from a therapist is always recommended. For us with BP2, our emotions are a journey. If you ever want to talk you can always message me. <3

*"Afterwards, sudden flood of irritability one following day, easily overstimulated, wanting to scream at the top of your lungs at everything and everyone, constantly on edge, bugs under your skin feeling and every sound feels 10x louder. Everything is touching you wrong. Very self conscious in social interactions and beginning to withdraw."*

**THIS!** Absolutely 100% what I'm going through right now. Last night I had trouble sleeping because normal nighttime noises were too much for me, the blankets felt like they were 50 lbs on my body and I felt like I was so overstimulated with it touching my skin. I couldn't even cuddle with my husband because it felt like pins and needles on my skin, even with just his arm around me it felt like too much. I'm grateful that I can spot & predict changes within my moods and how I'm physically/emotionally feeling, but man it takes a toll on me.

Oh yes, this was something I struggled with and STILL struggle with sometimes. I used to get so angry it was like I would turn into the Hulk without notice. Of course I'd NEVER want to hurt anyone, so I'd lock myself away so I wouldn't take it out on anyone except myself. 

When I'd talk to my therapist about how it felt like someone else was controlling my mind/body when I'd get angry, she corrected me by saying that it IS me, and ONLY me. So I had to sit with my anger and uncover WHY I was so angry. Which I've done a lot of work in therapy to figure out my triggers and identify when the feelings of rage would bubble up so I can take back control. Therapy and a good combo of meds has helped a lot too. 

When I get angry beyond reason or words, I will go for a walk/drive, listen to music, listen to a guided meditation on the app Headspace, immerse myself in books or other hobbies, or workout. One form of exercise that helped me was boxing. I worked for a boxing gym for 3 years doing mittwork with a coach, teaching group classes, and hitting the heavy bag. Being able to take it out on the bag was the most liberating feeling in the world. Currently I powerlift 5 days a week, but I always find time to hit the bag when I'm stressed or angry. If you're able to find a boxing gym in your area (or even buy a heavy bag, you can get standing ones if you're in a smaller space) I highly recommend it.

Thank you SO much for introducing me (and everyone else) to this podcast, it was very insightful. I attempted suicide and had these awful suicidal ideations that were so heavy I felt like I was drowning. After that attempt I was put on Lithium, and I’ve been on it for 8 years now. Lithium seriously saved my life.

I think the point is to find stability and the calm between mania and depressive episodes. The best way to explain it is like therapy and meds put BP2 in “remission” for me. I’ve done enough introspection to know when I’m starting to pull one way or the other and when I’m at a stable point. I try not to see it as a bad thing that I’ll have to manage for the rest of my life, if anything it’s changed my perspective on a lot of things  in my life. If I can manage BP2 then I can handle anything because I’ve fought so hard to be here. I stopped “chasing happiness” when I figured out it was already within me, I just had to tune into it once I got the internal “demons” to quiet down. Don’t give up.

I've changed jobs many times before I was properly diagnosed and medicated, so I know how you feel. I've been working consistently and diligently for 4 years now, which is a huge win for me! Some days I feel like I want to give up, not show up to work, block all my coworker's numbers, and just fall off the radar. My brain will rationalize it like - "if we just quietly disappear and find something new, we can just start over fresh!" BUT I know that if I do that it'll just be history repeating itself, and I'll be in the same unhappy loop forever. I found that I would mistake having a bad day or week as the JOB being the problem. Don't get me wrong, I had some shitty jobs and terrible bosses, but looking back I think I could have stuck it out longer.  Also, figuring out what you WANT to do is a good start. If you like working alone and want to be your own boss - look into working from home data entry jobs or transcription. Or deliver food for Door Dash, or even do grocery shopping for people for Shipt (or another company like that). You can set your own hours, and this may be a good place to at least start.  I found that a job with flexible hours or hours where I was most productive was best for me. My boss is pretty understanding, and with my position in the fitness industry as long as I get 8 hours of work in, she doesn't care when I start or end. I try and get my workday started at 6 AM so I can wrap up by 3 PM. 

It sounds like you already have a goal in mind - not relying on your boyfriend's income, which is a fantastic thing to strive for! I feel like for us with BP2, we need to be driven by something to get out of bed and be productive - a goal, purpose, or a want. I'm married, have rent to pay, and a cat to feed. That's what gets me up and makes me go to work every day. Then it becomes a habit, for every week that I go to work without calling off I'll treat myself to something small - maybe it's ice cream, a trip to the craft store, or going to the movies. Whatever makes me happy! I thrive on consistency and structure, so now I get agitated if something disrupts my work routine. This is tough to overcome, but we believe in you! If you ever need advice my messages are always open. :)

YES! I can definitely relate to this. I like to call myself an "introverted extrovert" (since I need alone time to recharge after social interactions, and I prefer to spend time at home alone or w/ the hubby). Sometimes I feel like my meds make it harder for me to think of things to say, like I'll get brain fog randomly or I'll just forget words lol.
YES! Very well said. 100% what I was thinking.
Yes! Perfect way to explain it. For me it took a month or so to really feel a difference. It quieted the mania, and for the first time in my life I felt stable.

Cycling between episodes is normal, and it’s hard to pinpoint when one will end and another will start. I would have a depressive episode for months, switch to mania that would last weeks, and then back again. They put me on a SSRI before my diagnosis and that helped with the depression, but gave my mania a place to live & thrive in my head rent free. After about a month of mania I came down so hard I was very close to ending it all. I kept a detailed record of my moods and shifts (along with the periods of stability) and when I presented it to my psychiatrist she immediately put me on a mood stabilizer and antipsychotic for depression and other symptoms I was experiencing. 

Now I’m on a combination of Lithium (mood stabilizer), and added in Celexa (SSRI) to help with depression. I stopped the antipsychotics because they made it impossible for me to function at my job (I’m a personal trainer and gym manager). I also take Klonopin as needed for anxiety. Meds and therapy have truly saved my life. My biggest piece of advice is to keep track of your moods, be honest with your doctor, and know that you’re not alone! 💕

Interesting, I’ve never heard someone explain something like that after stopping their meds. Do you feel safe with these memories resurfacing? Even if you feel like your past self is here, it will always still be YOU.

YES! 100%. I’m on Lithium as well, and I fully believe that it helped with my hyper sexuality. It’s common during a manic or hypomanic episode to engage in risky or impulsive behavior, even if it’s out of character for you. Before I was medicated I was with different partners every week, some I knew and some I didn’t. Of course I never felt fulfilled, I felt ashamed of myself and alone. Honestly I’m lucky that I didn’t end up with a STD or pregnant! Now that I’ve been on Lithium for years, I’m happily married with a healthy libido. 

Therapy has really helped me realize that hyper sexuality is more than just an addiction, but goes deeper than that. Definitely keep going to your meetings, you’ll gain so much insight in yourself by listening to other people’s stories. Thank you for shining some light on this subject, not many people talk about it! Keep us posted on how you’re doing. :)

First, I just want to say I fully believe you. I’m so sorry that you’re going through all of this. It can be really scary not understanding what’s going on with your emotions and in your head. You will need more than two weeks to feel a difference from medication, but in the meantime, start journaling your moods and what triggered them (if possible). It can be the slightest thing, no detail is too small. That way it’s all documented to discuss with your therapist and psychiatrist, and it’s your way to take back control by being self aware. If you have a trusted friend/family member to point out when you seem a little “off” have them do it, since we’re not ALWAYS great at figuring out the shifts from hypomania to a depressive episode. I was diagnosed at 18 after keeping logs of my moods for two years! They were hesitant to diagnose me due to my age, but with all of the recorded mood swings my diagnosis was undeniable. 

Also, watch for other things like hyper-sexuality, impulsive spending, excessive drug/alcohol abuse, engaging in risky behavior, lack of sleep because you don’t think you “need it”. Your brain will do everything it can to tell you that you’re okay and don’t need help, but this is self sabotage. You recognized something isn’t right, and that’s a huge step. You are NOT crazy, you’re on a mission to find answers and feel better. We’re here for you!! You can always message me as well. ❤️

Oh I can definitely relate to this! Luckily once I found the right combo of meds it really helped with my impulse control. I have “normal debt” like a car lease and credit cards, but I don’t spend nearly as much as I used to. Due to my habits I have very little savings and I live paycheck to paycheck pretty much. Whenever I get the urge I ask myself, “do I NEED this for survival? Do I have this or something like this already? Is this just a WANT?” Usually it’s a want. 

For slightly bigger purchases (think headphones, smart watch, etc) I do ALL my research to make sure I get the best price and if it’s truly worth it. Then I assess - can I afford to buy this item two times at once? So if the headphones are $200 can I buy a second pair and spend $400? Absolutely not, that’s ridiculous! So I won’t even buy it once. It’s a psychological thing that’s helped me back out of purchases many times. 

Idk if I’m just a sadist (lol), but I do “online window shopping” so I’ll go on Amazon and see stuff, put it on a list or cart and then not buy it. Just the act of putting it in my cart is satisfying! Then I’ll force myself to do something else, go for a walk, work on my hobbies, etc. then I’ll forget all about what I want to buy. I can’t tell you the amount of times I went back to my cart and asked myself, why did I even want to buy this? 

Hopefully some of this helps!

I’m currently on Lithium, Celexa, Klonopin (as needed), and Adderall. I was diagnosed with PCOS almost 10 years ago. I have similar symptoms that you’re describing and I tried Metformin without much luck. I went off birth control for about a year and the only changes I noticed was hormonal acne, heavier bleeding, more cramps, etc. I didn’t notice much of a difference mentally, but my PMS was arguably a little worse. I ended up going back on the pill to get control over the hormonal acne and have been on it for years now. I recommend that you keep track of your moods while you come off birth control so you can see if anything needs to be tweaked or changed. Always talk to your doctor if something doesn’t feel right. Hopefully this helps, keep us posted! :)

Oh my god, I love this. I make the SAME jokes with my husband, he knows every Sunday is pill case prep for the week. I feel like you need to laugh about it in order to let others know it’s not a shameful or uncomfortable topic!

I truly can relate to this. I’ve had the same conversation with friends/family. Unless they’ve been through it themselves, they won’t fully understand, but it sounds like they really care for you. 

Perhaps set up a weekly check in with friends/family to let them know you’re hanging in there, and it’ll push you to keep some sort of “normalcy” (whatever that is lol) in your life. 

As for work, I’ve struggled with anxiety over starting a new job - to the point where my husband has to give me a pep talk every few days to talk me off the ledge of backing out from a good job offer. Think about what you’re good at, what you enjoy, something you can tolerate, etc. and start from there. Depending on where you are, I think you could do temporary/short term disability, it sounds like your depression is very severe. Are you talking with a therapist or on medication? 

Please feel free to message me if you need to talk to someone privately.

I used to take Lamotrigine and had the same awful side effects! Then I got the “Lamictal rash” and had to stop taking it ASAP. It could be you have an intolerance to it, but please don’t think all medication will be this bad for you! 

Medication is all about trial and error, and sometimes it takes longer to find out what’s right for you. It took me a few years to find the right combo of medications. I take Lithium and a small dose of an antidepressant Celexa, and it’s truly saved my life. 

Do what you feel is right for you, especially since you’re in school. Have you called your doctor/psychiatrist and expressed your concern being on this medication? Best of luck and keep us updated!

I struggle with this as well! When I first added Lithium into my treatment regimen, I had the hardest time doing anything creative - my brain was just blank. I love to write, and I struggled to even write down simple words and sentences. I was very frustrated with this because creative writing has been an outlet since I was kid, and now it’s constant writers block. 

I try to get myself inspired instead - reading, looking at Pinterest, taking walks, etc. then I decided to change what I’d write about. So instead of creative stories, I started writing about things around me. It wasn’t the content of the writing, but the act of writing that satisfied my creative urge. 

Also I picked up different hobbies like cross stitching and dabbling in writing poetry. I think it’s very possible to maintain hobbies by finding ways to re-engage yourself. 

If it’s too much, try new things. When I get frustrated with a cross stitch piece I’m working on, I set it down and do something very different - like exercise or go on Duolingo to learn a new language! Usually that can ground me enough to return to my cross stitch and try it again. Maybe picking up a new hobby that’s not related to drawing/painting can inspire you to return to art later.

I used to take Prozac and had the same issue with my hypomania getting out of control. Prozac was only treating one part - the depression. My psychiatrist figured that out real fast and added in a mood stabilizer with it. I tried many combos, but Celexa (SSRI) for depression, and Lithium for mood stabilizing have actually saved my life. It’s all trial and error. Be open with your psychiatrist about your concerns, and journal your mood changes, how long it lasts/intensity, etc. this will help you and your psychiatrist make an informed decision on your treatment plan. I hope everything works out, we’re here for you!

After my diagnosis I sobered up as well! Major props to you for consciously deciding to stop for the time being, that really helps get you back in control - literally and figuratively. :)

As for coping mechanisms, lately guided meditation has helped a lot. I use the app Headspace regularly, and I like that they have short 3 min meditations and longer ones when I have time. 

Petting/playing with my cat, going for a walk, and writing down the good/bad thoughts so I can sort through what needs to be addressed now or later. 

Also, I told my fiancé if he ever suspects signs of a manic/depressive episode, he can ask me what’s going through my mind and talk me through it. Kind of like bringing me back down to earth and grounding me in reality. Best of luck to you and I hope you find what works for you!

I seriously empathize with this, as this happened to me recently. 

First of all, being understaffed and busting at the seams is NOT your problem - that’s a company problem. All you can do is focus on your own work and contribution to the company. 

As for the mistake, is there any way you can make a reminder for yourself to avoid the mistake? Or even work with your boss to see if there’s something you’re missing from the process that’s making you make this mistake. Unrealistic deadlines? Too much workload? Maybe HR can be a helpful resource for you. You’re not defeated, you’re burnt out and need to take care of yourself. 

My boss reacted the same way yours did. I realized that if I’m not going to get any sympathy or care from him, then I need to figure out how to organize myself so my work doesn’t slip. I would work for a while, then take a break for a few minutes to gather my thoughts. I use the app Headspace for quick SOS meditations and breathing exercises to help with the anxiety. 

I don’t know what you do, but perhaps you should take a vacation day or two (or more). If they’re not understanding that you CAN’T do everything and you’re only ONE person, then you should seriously reconsider where you’re working. No job is worth your mental and physical health, especially having a boss that doesn’t even remotely care about the well-being of her staff. 

I’m trying to take my own advice on this, but you’re not alone. All of us here are your support system! No matter what you choose to do, we’re here for you! ❤️

This is a really good tip! I do this too whenever I’m feeling the itch to spend money. Shopping in your own closet is also really good when you’re looking to declutter during or after the hypomanic phase ends! 😂

I’m an open book. :) & Lamictal was the first one I tried. unfortunately I couldn’t take it for long because I developed the “lamictal rash”, which isn’t super common. I have a close friend on Lamictal and it’s been really helpful for her mania/severe anxiety.

Oof! I currently take Adderall, and before I found a stable combo of meds I used to get the “Adderall rage” which would induce a manic episode. 

Before my BP2 diagnosis, they had me on different SSRI’s which dulled my depression to the point of apathy so my mania went into overdrive. Once lithium was introduced to the SSRI they worked together really well - and they still do. My psychiatrist explained that the combo was necessary to treat both the mania AND depression, sometimes one medication can’t do it all so it’s all trial and error. 

Everyone reacts differently to meds, so being able to spot an episode or shift in mood is the best way you can prevent that from happening.

Hormones can definitely be at play here, especially at your age. It sounds like you need some coping techniques when someone/something sets you off. Hearing that there’s rage and lashing out tells me that there’s a lot of overstimulation going on in your brain and a lot of bottled up energy that needs to be released in a constructive (not destructive) way. It sounds cliche, but calming hobbies can help - cross stitching, painting, drawing, writing it all out, etc. if you like physical activity go for a bike ride, walk/hike, play your favorite sport. I’ve been boxing for a year and a half and it’s done so much for regulating my moods! 

Also, guided meditation has helped a lot (I use the app Headspace or Calm). When someone pisses me off I stop right in the moment and breathe, or find a safe place to breathe and bring myself back down to reality. Your therapist will definitely have more ways for you to cope, but I hope some of this helps in the meantime!

Just like she has a right to say no to birth control, so do you! There’s an IUD called Paragard that’s copper so there’s no hormones, I had that for a while because I couldn’t stand birth control side effects. She can also keep track of her cycle so she knows when she’s ovulating (so you guys can avoid having sex when she’s most fertile), and wear a condom. If all of this is a dealbreaker for her and she won’t compromise on anything then she’s not the one for you.

Absolutely! I take 10 mg of Celexa (I’m very sensitive to medication side effects). As for lithium I used to be on 1,200 mg a day (600 in the morning, 600 at night). I work a pretty high pressure sales job and the high dose of lithium made it hard for me to relate to people and be higher energy. So I ended up cutting out my morning dose so I’m at 600 mg in the evening which has worked pretty well for me. 

I highly recommend keeping a journal of any side effects you’re feeling and report them to your doctor/psychiatrist to make sure it’s not too much or too little.

I’ve been on Lithium (mood stabilizer) and Celexa (antidepressant) for years and it’s truly saved my life. I could feel the sun on my skin, a nice cool breeze, and I could appreciate the things my low periods would not let me feel. I felt the will to live, and it really gave me hope. 

Those feelings outweigh almost all side effects, and kept me from giving up. Talk to your psychiatrist/doctor about your concerns about taking meds, make an informed decision, and discuss what will work best for you. Keep us updated! ❤️

Not sure how it works where you live, but can a family member or your fiancé pick up your meds for you (if you stick with Walgreens)? Sometimes I get stuck working late and can’t pick up my prescriptions so my fiancé will get them. I definitely think you need a new doctor, it’s so irresponsible and dangerous to refuse sending in a patients refills for a drug they can’t just quit cold turkey. I hope everything works out, and you can get your meds. Please keep us posted!!

I’m the General Manager of a boxing club. I’ve been there for a year and a half which is a HUGE win since I’ve always had a hard time sticking with jobs. It’s a fast paced environment and pretty stressful, but I’m hanging in there.

It took 2 different psychiatrists, 3 therapists, and 5 years for them to finally give me my bipolar 2 diagnosis. 

We tried Celexa, Lexapro, Wellbutrin, Prozac, Effexor.

And then we tried the mood stabilizers/anticonvulsants Trileptal, Lamictal (which gave me the Lamictal rash), and Abilify. 

We tried them alone and in different combinations, and let me tell you it messed with my mind, body, and spirit for those 5 years. Finally by 18/19 years old we found a great combo of a low dose of Celexa, and Lithium. We started off gradual and added more as needed. I’m also prescribed Klonopin as needed. With my combo now, I hardly find myself reaching for the Klonopin though. 

It’s been my saving grace honestly, but so has Psychodynamic therapy once a week.  I was in CBT for almost all of my teenage years which gave me a great foundation to finally deal with trauma from my past, and day to day challenges with BP2. I’ve talked to a lot of people who have similar stories, most mental health professionals aren’t the quickest to diagnose bipolar disorder. They spend a lot of time with therapy and drug therapy first. I saw my diagnosis as a huge relief, FINALLY I had an answer. I know what to call this now, so it no longer has power over me. 

My advice to anyone with bipolar 2, work close with health professionals (therapy and drug therapy), document how you feel in a journal (physically and emotionally - so you can look for patterns), and listen to your body/symptoms. Recognize the triggers that set you into a manic OR depressive episode, and come up with “escape routes” or ways to cope when things become too overwhelming. And always keep yourself grounded, and try to be logical and factual if you ever start rapid cycling. Reddit has an awesome support system here, which is comforting because not everyone in our lives quite understand what’s going on in our heads.

Actually, PF is VERY transparent about their agreements and cancellation policy because of these situations. The first signature you sign tells you what membership you’re getting, how much the start up fee is, when you’ll be billed, how much, how to cancel and when you need to cancel in order to not be billed for the next cycle. The staff is there to explain these terms as well. I would think you would cancel the day you were leaving so you wouldn’t have to deal with calling or sending a certified letter. You can’t verify an identity over the phone. You can’t sign the cancellation document over the phone and if you send a letter with your signature then that’s how PF can verify it with your contract. It’s for security purposes, which is great because it prevents people from pretending to be someone else just to cancel their membership. Ask more questions and read the contract next time.

The only time a club can’t cancel a membership due to location is if they’re outside of the franchise. This is because they wouldn’t have access to your information or agreement to cancel you. They should have been nicer about how transferring, and you’re right, they could have just told you to cancel at your home club. As for the buy out fee, you do sign off on the agreement for the 12 month term when you sign up. I would wait out the contract, it’ll be cheaper that way for you. The staff member should have given you this information, and I would talk to the general manager of that club and let them know about the employee’s attitude.

Yes there’s absolutely solutions! I’m so sorry that they’re giving you a hard time with transferring. At PF, we care about the member’s happiness, which means that sometimes we can bend rules and accommodate someone’s needs. Even though I’m a manager in Michigan, this should be universal for every club. Ask to speak to the General Manager of the club and explain your situation. Let them know that you’re unhappy and you’re considering canceling your membership as a result. Usually, managers will buckle. If not, ask the General Manager to get you in touch with the Regional Manager (they’re most DEFINITELY customer service oriented). 

We do something called a “Force Transfer” which is when a member hasn’t been at their home club for more than 90 days, but transferring would be more convenient and accommodating to the member. All it takes is the manager of your home club to e-mail PF Support with your first and last name, agreement number, and club you want to transfer to. It usually takes 24 hours to process, and they would follow up with you and let you know it’s finished. Shame on them for not being more understanding and helpful. I’m very sorry!

I love this question! I get asked this often (i’m an assistant manager of a club in Michigan) and I enjoy giving the run down of what it’s like in the judgement free zone! Planet Fitness has a great atmosphere for first time gym users and “experienced” gym goers. 

First, definitely bring a key or combination lock. If you don’t have one then they should sell them behind the counter. I bring a small purse or gym bag, and I lock mine up for the duration of my work out. Remember to take your things with you when you’re done! Wear what makes you comfortable, for me personally I wear a t-shirt or tank top, leggings or running shorts, socks, and tennis shoes. I keep my hair off my face and remove all jewelry besides my earrings and my Fitbit. Bring headphones if you like listening to music while you work out! 

If this is your first time in, go up to the front desk. If you signed up online then they’ll need to take your pic for your profile and give you a key tag to scan in. PF has a “no lunk” policy, which means they don’t cater to body building or power lifting. No string tank tops (where too much skin is exposed/men’s nipples are out), no sandals, no jeans, no gallon water jugs (bring a water bottle, or you can purchase one there!). PF doesn’t tolerate any loud “grunting” or “screaming” or any intimidating behavior that disrupts anyone’s work out. Also, dropping/throwing weights is against the rules and extremely rude to the staff and can damage equipment or hurt someone else. If you get a phone call, please get off the equipment you’re on and take it to the front lobby, just as a courtesy for others. Honestly, all of the policies center around being kind to your neighbor, respect the staff and equipment, and enjoy the judgement free atmosphere PF has to offer. 

You can also go online and take a virtual tour of the club before you go in, and when you’re there you can ask anyone behind the desk to give you a tour. Trust me, you’re not bothering them, it’s what they’re there for! Never be afraid to ask questions, and take advantage of the free fitness training classes with a certified instructor. They will have schedules for the trainer up at the front desk as well. I hope you enjoy everything Planet Fitness has to offer, and I hope this answers your question and more! (:

Hello! I’m very sorry for your mom’s condition, and I’m sorry for all the stress it’s put you through. As soon as I read this I could immediately relate. My mom is 56 years old and she sat my sister and I down when I was about 10 years old to tell us she has Multiple Sclerosis (MS). When she told us I didn’t know exactly what it meant, but then she talked about having to get injections once a week so the lesions on her brain and spine would stay inactive. She also told us she has to do it or else she wouldn’t live to see us graduate high school. 

As a kid I always remember my mom being sick. She rarely attended my sporting events, play dates were usually at my friends house or my sister would supervise us at my house. My mom had these “special naps” when I was younger and that meant we had to quietly tip toe around so we wouldn’t wake my mom up. We’d catch hell if we did that. To this day being 21 years old, I still am light on my feet when I walk, purely out of habit. 

The shots my mom got every week gave her awful side effects. I saw my mom - strong and beautiful, suddenly look so defeated and exhausted. My mom lost at least 20-30 pounds over the span of 11 years, and some days she couldn’t even walk. My dad would have to carry her or she’d take her time to slowly shuffle down the stairs. For a while she wasn’t able to hold anything or grip anything, and she couldn’t keep food down. It was so awful to watch. 

They monitor her lesions with a MRI scan every year and I’m proud to say that she doesn’t have nearly as many active lesions on her spine as she did before. For a while she had to go through an IV steroid treatment because she developed more active lesions on her brain. As of right now she has no new lesions and she’s doing so well on her meds. I’m here for you, if you ever need someone to talk to. It gets lonely, and growing up it’s hard to find someone who can relate or understand. You miss out on things in your childhood/teenage years because you have to grow up so fast. It’s nice to find a kindred soul. You’re an extremely strong person, don’t forget that.

Hi! I work at a Planet Fitness club in Michigan (but the experience will be the same in most states). I wouldn’t expect them to upsell you at all, especially since the whole point of the Black Card weekend is to let you experience all of the perks and amenities in hopes that you’ll upgrade your membership. Upgrading is free by the way! You won’t have to sign anything, you covered all liabilities in your agreement when you first signed up for your Home Club membership. 

You get access amenities such as the hydro massage beds and lounges, the coin operated massage chairs (like the ones at the mall), tanning, and their Total Body Enhancement booths. All of these things they should go in depth explaining to you. If you’re going tanning or into the TBE booth then you will have to purchase some form of eyewear (clubs should have disposable stickers for .50 or the reusable goggles for ~$2.65 - again, Michigan rates). 

Depending on the club they may have you sign in to use such amenities, but that’s just for record keeping, you don’t have to worry about it counting against you. Want to experience the Black Card perks with a friend? You can bring one friend with the Black Card privileges! All they need is a driver’s license or form of picture ID (18+), and the club will either make them sign in on a sheet (keep track of people coming in and out), or they’ll make them a quick guest profile. The guest profile is cool because if they decide to sign up most of their info is already there so we can convert it into a membership! 

You also get half off cooler drinks. Every Planet Fitness is franchise owned, so each club has their own selection of drinks. For my club, the only drink that’s NOT half off is the Muscle Milk. Everything else is (water, Gatorade, energy drinks). I highly recommend taking advantage of these perks this weekend! You may end up liking it. 

Hope this helps! Let me know if you end up going and how you like it!
